In March of this year, Apple announced the discontinuation of the Mac Pro and confirmed there were no plans to release new Mac Pro hardware.

A new Bloomberg report today further reveals the backstory of Apple's Mac Pro strategy, mentioning a surprising detail about the plan……

The inside story of Apple's shelved Mac Pro plans

In the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Mark Gurman points out that Apple internally "did not plan to abandon the Mac Pro from the start." Gurman again mentions a previously reported claim: Apple's original concept was to launch a chip called "Extreme" on top of the "Ultra" chip.

The report quoted: "It is understood that Apple had developed two chips, the M2 Extreme and M3 Extreme, but ultimately terminated the projects due to cost and demand considerations."

As for the specific Mac Pro hardware that was developed, Gurman said Apple had two models (internal codenames J170 and J190) in development at the time, but neither was ultimately released to market.

The most intriguing detail in the report is that one of the models used an Intel processor:

Apple ultimately discontinued the Mac Pro in March, removed it from its official website, and directed buyers to purchase the Mac Studio instead. Although the discontinuation had long been foreshadowed, it still marks the quiet end of an era for Mac Pro enthusiasts.

Apple has abandoned the Mac Pro product line and chosen not to launch an "Extreme" chip in the Apple Silicon era. What do you think of this decision? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
